examples.en: A wedding photo is hanging on the living room wall.
We went to a studio to take wedding photos.
Mom was really pretty in her wedding photo.

examples.ko: 결혼사진은 결혼식 전에 미리 찍기도 해요.
examples.en: Wedding photos are sometimes taken in advance, before the ceremony.
Is our whole family in the wedding photo?

examples.ko: 새로 찍은 결혼사진으로 휴대폰 배경을 바꿨어요.
examples.en: I changed my phone wallpaper to our newly taken wedding photo.

explain: 결혼식 날 찍은 사진과 스튜디오에서 따로 찍은 사진 둘 다 가리킬 수 있어요. 일상에서는 '웨딩 사진'이라고도 해요. '결혼사진을 찍다', '결혼사진을 보다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It can refer both to photos taken on the wedding day and to photos taken separately at a studio. In daily talk people also say '웨딩 사진'. You use it like '결혼사진을 찍다' or '결혼사진을 보다'.

examples.en: The graphics in this game are really pretty.
I watched a movie made with computer graphics.
The screen is smooth since I changed the graphics card.
My younger brother studies graphic design.
The news had a graphic, so I understood the content.

examples.ko: 이 앱은 그래픽보다 사용법이 더 중요해요.
examples.en: For this app, ease of use matters more than graphics.

explain: 게임이나 영상 화면의 그림 품질은 '그래픽이 좋다/별로다'처럼 말해요. 그림을 설계하는 일은 '디자인', 사진의 선명함은 '화질'이라 쓰는 자리가 달라요. 컴퓨터 부품 이름은 '그래픽 카드' 또는 '그래픽카드'로 써요.
explain_en: For the picture quality of games and videos, people say the graphics are good or so-so. Designing images is '디자인' and photo sharpness is '화질', so the words are used in different spots. The computer part is written '그래픽 카드' or '그래픽카드'.

examples.ko: 저는 대학교에서 오 년 동안 러시아어를 공부했어요.
examples.en: I studied Russian at university for five years.
Russian letters are very different from ours.
My friend sang a song in Russian for me.

examples.ko: 러시아어를 할 줄 알면 여행에 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: Knowing Russian helps when you travel.
The Russian class is on Thursday evening.
This book was translated from Russian into Korean.

explain: '러시아어를 배우다/하다/공부하다'처럼 써요. 러시아어는 '키릴 문자'라는 다른 글자를 써서 처음에는 글자부터 새로 익혀야 해요. 영어, 중국어, 일본어처럼 나라 이름 뒤에 '-어'를 붙여 말 이름을 만들어요.
explain_en: Say 러시아어를 배우다/하다/공부하다. Russian uses a different script called Cyrillic (키릴 문자), so you start by learning new letters. Like 영어, 중국어 and 일본어, the language name is the country name plus -어.

examples.ko: 봄이 오면 맛있는 봄나물을 먹을 수 있어요.
examples.en: When spring comes, you can eat delicious spring greens.
I bought a bag of spring greens at the market.
I made bibimbap with spring greens.
Spring greens are blanched and then seasoned by hand.

examples.ko: 봄나물에는 비타민이 많아서 피로 회복에 좋아요.
examples.en: Spring greens are rich in vitamins and good for recovering from fatigue.
This restaurant's spring greens set meal is popular.

explain: 냉이, 달래, 쑥처럼 봄에 먹는 나물을 묶어서 부르는 말이에요. 산이나 들에서 '캐다'라고 하고, 먹을 때는 '무치다'를 많이 써요. 봄에는 식당 메뉴판에도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a collective name for greens eaten in spring, such as 냉이, 달래 and 쑥. You '캐다' them in hills or fields, and '무치다' is the common verb for seasoning them. They often show up on restaurant menus in spring.

examples.en: I'm the vice class president of our class.
The vice class president ran the meeting in place of the class president.
We elected the vice class president by vote.
The vice class president helps the class president collect homework.
My friend was chosen as vice class president and is happy.
I'm thinking of running in the vice class president election.

explain: 학교 한 반에서 '반장'을 돕는 학생이에요. '부-'는 '부회장', '부사장'처럼 한 단계 아래 직책 앞에 붙어요. 반장이 없을 때 회의를 대신 이끌기도 해요.
explain_en: This is the student who assists the '반장' in a school class. The prefix '부-' goes before ranks one step below, as in '부회장' and '부사장'. When the '반장' is absent, the '부반장' may lead the class meeting instead.

examples.en: I watch the news in the living room every evening.
Many people watched that broadcast.

examples.ko: 아이들이 텔레비전을 너무 오래 시청하면 눈이 아파요.
examples.en: If kids watch TV for too long, their eyes hurt.

examples.ko: 이 영상은 무료로 시청할 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can watch this video for free.
Let's talk after we watch the drama together.

examples.ko: 퇴근 후에 야구 중계를 시청하는 게 제 취미예요.
examples.en: Watching baseball broadcasts after work is my hobby.

explain: TV, 뉴스, 영상을 볼 때 쓰는데, 방송 안내나 글에 잘 나와요. 말할 때는 '보다'가 훨씬 자연스러워서 '뉴스 봤어요?'라고 해요. 보는 사람은 '시청자'예요. 소리가 같은 '시청'은 도시의 관청을 가리켜서 '서울시청'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is used for watching TV, news, or videos, and shows up in broadcast notices and writing. In speech '보다' is far more natural: '뉴스 봤어요?' A viewer is a '시청자'. The homophone '시청' means city hall, as in '서울시청'.

p.n: The replacement means following the news attentively, not specifically watching it on a screen.

examples.ko: 고등학생 때 연애편지를 처음 써 봤어요.
examples.en: I wrote a love letter for the first time in high school.
An old love letter turned up in the desk drawer.
I wrote a love letter all night and my face turned red.
These days people send messages instead of love letters.

examples.ko: 그는 매일 밤 연애편지를 한 장씩 썼대요.
examples.en: I heard he wrote one love letter every night.
The handwriting in the love letter is so pretty.

explain: '러브레터'라고도 하지만 일상 대화에서는 '연애편지'를 많이 써요. '연애편지를 쓰다, 보내다, 받다'처럼 말해요. 손으로 쓴 편지는 '손편지'라고 해요.
explain_en: '러브레터' is also used, but in everyday talk '연애편지' is common. You say '연애편지를 쓰다/보내다/받다' (write/send/receive). A handwritten letter is called a '손편지'.

examples.ko: 잠자기 전에 아이에게 이야기책을 읽어 줘요.
examples.en: I read a storybook to my child before bed.
I borrowed a fun storybook from the library.
The pictures in the storybook are really pretty.

examples.ko: 어렸을 때 할머니 댁에서 이야기책을 많이 봤어요.
examples.en: As a child, I read lots of storybooks at my grandmother's house.

examples.ko: 이야기책은 글씨가 크고 쉬워서 한국어 공부에 좋아요.
examples.en: Storybooks have big, easy text, so they're good for studying Korean.
I don't know where this storybook went.

explain: 아이용 책을 말할 때는 '동화책'도 많이 써요. '이야기책'은 옛날이야기나 소설처럼 이야기가 중심인 책을 넓게 가리켜요. '읽다'와 '읽어 주다'를 같이 알아 두면 좋아요.
explain_en: For children's books, people also say '동화책'. '이야기책' covers books centered on a story more broadly, like old tales or novels. It's good to learn it with both '읽다' (read) and '읽어 주다' (read to someone).

examples.en: I saw the Seoul night view from Namsan Tower.
You go up to the top of the tower by elevator.
That tall tower is a famous tourist spot.
I took photos with my friends in front of the tower.
A new tower has been built in this city.
Inside the tower there is an observatory and a restaurant.

explain: 옛 절에 있는 돌탑이나 전통 건축물은 '탑', 현대의 높은 전망 건물은 '타워'라고 불러요. '남산타워', '롯데월드타워'처럼 이름 뒤에 붙는 일이 많아요. 방송이나 통신용 높은 건물에도 '타워'를 써요.
explain_en: Stone pagodas at old temples and traditional structures are '탑', while tall modern observation buildings are 'tower'. It usually attaches to a name, as in '남산타워' or '롯데월드타워'. It is also used for tall broadcast and communication structures.

examples.en: I go to a music festival in summer.

examples.ko: 이 페스티벌은 삼 일 동안 열려요.
examples.en: This festival runs for three days.
I bought film festival tickets in advance.
I am sad that the festival is over.
I went with friends to see the festival.
The roads are very jammed because of the festival.

explain: '축제'가 더 일상적인 우리말이고, 페스티벌은 음악·영화처럼 행사 이름에 붙을 때 많이 써요. '대학 축제', '지역 축제'는 축제를 써요. '록 페스티벌'처럼 이름이 정해진 행사는 페스티벌 그대로 불러요.
explain_en: 축제 is the more everyday native word, while 페스티벌 is common in event names for music and film. Say 대학 축제 and 지역 축제 with 축제. Events with fixed names, like a rock festival, keep 페스티벌.
